content: 1. Amikacin, when used with amphotericin B deoxycholate, increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Concurrent use of amikacin and cidofovir also increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity and is contraindicated. 3. Amikacin and oral neomycin together elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity, making this combination contraindicated. 4. Amikacin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Co-administration of amikacin and bacitracin raises the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Amikacin reduces the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 7. Bumetanide and amikacin together increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, heightening the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Amikacin reduces the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine within 14 days of antibiotic use. 9. Amikacin enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Alternative drugs should be considered. 10. Amikacin and iodinated contrast media both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Co-administration of amikacin and cyclosporine increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Ethacrynic acid and amikacin together increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Furosemide and amikacin also increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, with a heightened risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Amikacin and ioversol both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Amikacin reduces the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 16. Amikacin enhances the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Alternative drugs should be considered. 17. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Amikacin enhances the effects of rapacuronium, rocuronium, and succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Alternative drugs should be considered. 19. Co-administration of amikacin and tacrolimus increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Amikacin and teicoplanin together increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Torsemide and amikacin increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Amikacin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 23. Amikacin enhances the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Alternative drugs should be considered. 24. Amikacin may potentiate the effects of botulinum toxins (e.g., abobotulinumtoxinA, incobotulinumtoxinA, onabotulinumtoxinA, prabotulinumtoxinA, rimabotulinumtoxinB) through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially causing excessive neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Co-administration of amikacin with nephrotoxic agents such as acyclovir, adefovir, carboplatin, colistin, cisplatin, foscarnet, gentamicin, methoxyflurane, oxaliplatin, paromomycin, pentamidine, polymyxin B, streptomycin, streptozocin, tenofovir DF, tobramycin, or vancomycin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 26. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of oral contraceptives (e.g., conjugated estrogens, estradiol, estrone, mestranol) by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional forms of birth control may be advisable. 27. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of certain vitamins and minerals (e.g., biotin, calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, cyanocobalamin) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of these agents. 28. Co-administration of amikacin with NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, aspirin, diclofenac, indomethacin, ketorolac) or COX-2 inhibitors (e.g., celecoxib) may increase amikacin levels by reducing renal clearance, particularly in preterm infants. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora, which is necessary for drug activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Co-administration of amikacin with magnesium supplements may increase the risk of neuromuscular weakness and respiratory effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of certain antibiotics (e.g., rifampin, clotrimazole) and antifungals (e.g., fluconazole, ketoconazole) through unknown mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Amikacin may interact synergistically with aztreonam against Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacteriaceae. This combination may be used therapeutically. 33. Co-administration of amikacin with drugs that affect renal clearance (e.g., entecavir) may increase serum concentrations of either drug. Use caution and monitor closely. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions between amikacin and various drugs, emphasizing the risks and necessary precautions.
